get.summary: Read raw telemetry records
get.description: Unaggregated good-quality observations of one parameter (diagnostics excluded), newest first, in pages of `page_size` 1 to 100 (default 50) up to a total `limit` of 1 to 5000 (default 500). The window is at most 31 days. `cursor` is signed and bound to the query; pass `meta.next_cursor` with the same query. 422 for an invalid window or a cursor the runtime rejects (under `errors.runtime`); 503 when the runtime is unavailable.

get.summary: Read the event feed
get.description: `integration-event.v1` envelopes after `cursor` (from the start of the journal without one), in commit order, `limit` 1 to 100 (default 100). Pages skip events for devices not granted to the application, so save `next_cursor` even from an empty page. The feed is at least once: deduplicate by event `id`. Cursors are encrypted and bound to the organization, the application and its grant revision; a token rotation keeps them. Needs `events:read` and either `alerts:read` or `geofences:read`, each on both the application and the token. 409 after a grant change (rebuild from a fresh checkpoint); 422 for invalid input, an unreadable cursor or another application's cursor.

post.summary: Create a geofence and activate it
post.description: Saves a new geofence (revision 1) with one workflow per assigned device, then starts their activation and returns 202 with the activation to poll. Needs `geofences:activate` and `geofences:manage`. Idempotent on `operation_uuid`. 403 when an assigned device is not granted; 404 when an assigned device has no location binding; 409 when `operation_uuid` was used for a different request or `expected_revision` is not 0; 422 for invalid input, or when the runtime rejects the geofence (a message, or `errors.runtime`); 503 when the runtime is unavailable.

put.summary: Update a geofence and activate it
put.description: Saves a new revision of the geofence (name, geometry and the full set of assignments; devices left out are removed), then starts the activation and returns 202 with the activation to poll. post.summary: Signed delivery of one integration event
post.description:
Sent to the application's webhook endpoint (HTTPS on port 443, one per application, which must grant `events:read` and `alerts:read`) for each event on its granted devices, in journal order, one delivery at a time and at most one send per second per endpoint. The body is the same envelope the feed returns.

**Signature.** `X-Iot-Signature` is `v1=` followed by the hex HMAC-SHA256 of `X-Iot-Timestamp + "." + X-Iot-Delivery-Id + "." + raw body`, keyed with the endpoint's signing secret. Verify it over the raw bytes before parsing, reject a timestamp more than 300 seconds from your clock, and deduplicate by event `id` before returning 2xx: a valid signature can be replayed.

**Retries.** A 2xx response confirms delivery. Timeouts (3 s to connect, 5 s to transfer), network errors, 408, 425, 429 and 5xx are retried after 10 s, 30 s, 2 min and 10 min, up to five attempts within 24 hours; any other status, including a redirect, fails the delivery at once. A delivery that is still being retried holds back newer ones for that endpoint. Saving the endpoint rotates the secret, cancels pending deliveries and starts at the current head of the journal; recover gaps through the feed. Revoking the application or changing its grants disables the endpoint.

parameters.name: X-Iot-Delivery-Id
parameters.description: The delivery's UUID, the same on every attempt.

parameters.name: X-Iot-Timestamp
parameters.description: Unix seconds when this attempt was signed.

parameters.name: X-Iot-Signature
parameters.description: `v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256>`.

2XX.description: Delivered. Return it only after recording the event `id`.

default.description: Not delivered. 408, 425, 429 and 5xx are retried; any other status fails the delivery.

NoStore.description: Responses to authenticated integration requests are never cached. The header also carries `private`.

Conflict.description: The request conflicts with the current state, for example a stale revision.

CsrfExpired.description: The anti-forgery token is missing or has expired. Fetch `GET /sanctum/csrf-cookie` again and retry.

DraftConflict.description: The device-profile draft changed since the caller read it (`code: profile.draft_conflict`). Reload it before saving.

Forbidden.description: The caller is not allowed: not a member of the organization, missing a tenant or platform permission, or (integration API) an ability not granted on both the application and the token.

GrantChanged.description: The cursor can no longer be used: the application's grants changed, or the event history changed. Rebuild the projection from a fresh checkpoint.

NotFound.description: Not found: an unknown organization or resource, a resource in another organization or not granted to the application, or a malformed identifier (the route does not match).

RangeTimeout.description: A range read took longer than the runtime's limit. Choose a shorter range.

RuntimeUnavailable.description: The device runtime is not configured, unavailable, or could not complete the request.

ServiceUnavailable.description: A service the operation depends on, other than the device runtime, is not configured or unavailable: the AI provider, the broker, the adapter runtime or the public MQTT endpoint. The message says which.

TooManyRequests.description: A rate limit was reached; see `x-rate-limits` on the operation.

Unauthenticated.description: No valid credentials: no session (first-party API), or a missing, invalid, expired or revoked application token (integration API).

Unprocessable.description: The input failed validation (`errors` names the fields), or the request cannot be applied in the resource's current state (a message only, for example an archived device or a limit reached).

AlertIntegrationEvent.description: An alert was activated, cleared or acknowledged; `data` is the alert snapshot.

action_id.description: The action's identity, stable across retries.

name.description: The event name configured on the node.

CompactPage.description: Compact page metadata used by most paginated lists. Combine with `allOf` and an object that describes `data`. Some operations add fields to `meta`.

DraftConflictError.description: 409 when a device-profile draft changed since the caller read it.

ErrorMessage.description: The body of most error responses.

EventPage.description: A page of the event feed. Continue from `next_cursor` while `has_more` is true; when it is false, poll again later from `next_cursor`.

next_cursor.description: Save it even when `data` is empty; it moves past skipped events.

GeofenceActivationBatch.description: The activation of one geofence revision: one item per assignment to activate or remove. Poll it until `status` is no longer `pending`.

id.description: Pass as `item` to retry a failed item.

operation_uuid.description: The workflow deployment that applies this item.

GeofenceAssignment.description: One device assigned to the geofence, with its own workflow.

deployment_status.description: The assignment workflow's deployment status, for example `pending`, `active` or `inactive`.

source_event_uuid.description: The telemetry event that caused the transition, when there was one.

GeofenceGeometry.description: A GeoJSON Polygon with one ring of 4 to 257 positions.

GeofenceInput.description: A geofence to save and activate. Every assigned device must be granted to the application and have a location binding.

operation_uuid.description: Idempotency key and the activation's UUID. Repeating the same request returns the same result; reusing it for a different request returns 409.

expected_revision.description: The revision the client last read; a stale value returns 409. Defaults to 0 when creating (which must stay 0) and to the current revision when updating.

geometry.description: Only `type` and `coordinates`; any other member is rejected.

assignments.description: Devices to assign; each `device_uuid` at most once. Devices left out are removed.

GeofenceIntegrationEvent.description: A device entered or left a geofence (`entered`, `exited`), or its geofence rule activated or cleared (`wandering_started`, `wandering_resolved`).

GeofencePolicy.description: When a device counts as wandering outside the geofence.

GeofenceSaved.description: The saved geofence and the activation to poll.

IntegrationAbility.description: An ability granted to an application and to its token; an operation needs it on both. `events:read` also needs `alerts:read` or `geofences:read`; `geofences:activate` also needs `geofences:manage`.

IntegrationAlert.description: A snapshot of one alert episode. The same object is the `data` of the `alert.*.v1` events.

execution_stopped_reason.description: Why the alert's workflow stopped evaluating, for example `binding_changed`.

IntegrationDevice.description: A device granted to the application.

presence.description: `online`, `offline`, `unseen`, or `unknown` when the runtime's last online report is more than 20 seconds old. Presence is separate from data quality.

IntegrationEvent.description: `integration-event.v1`: one entry of the organization's event journal, from the feed or a webhook. `data` is a snapshot taken when the event was written; apply it as authoritative. Journal order is commit order, not event time. The same `id` can arrive more than once.

id.description: Stable across feed reads, webhook retries and redelivery.

recorded_at.description: When the event was written to the journal (not its commit time).

IntegrationEventType.description: Every event type the platform emits today. New types may be added within v1.

IntegrationGeofence.description: A geofence, with only the assignments of devices granted to the application.

LocationBindingVersion.description: An approved, immutable location binding and the version that carries it.

version_uuid.description: Pass as `version_uuid` to read a fix through this binding.

LocationMap.description: `location-map.v1`: positions and trails of the requested devices.

devices.description: One entry per requested device that has a location binding.

LocationMapDevice.description: The device runtime's map entry, passed through unchanged, plus `wandering`, `active_alert`, `assignment_status` and `deployment_status` added by the control plane.

latest.description: The latest fix through the device's binding, or `null` when there is none in retention.

condition.description: `unknown` unless the latest fix is live-eligible.

active.description: Whether the geofence rule's condition is active.

geometry.description: The geofence geometry of the device's active rule, or `null`.

segments.description: Runs of valid fixes; a gap longer than twice the binding's `max_age_seconds` starts a new segment. Empty unless trails were requested.

sampled.description: Whether the trail was thinned to at most 200 points.

wandering.description: Whether the device's geofence workflow has an active alert.

assignment_status.description: The geofence assignment's status, or `null` when the device has no assignment.

deployment_status.description: The assignment workflow's deployment status, or `null`.

ProfileValidationError.description: 422 for a device profile that failed validation or compilation.

pointer.description: JSON pointer into the profile definition.

ResourcePage.description: Full page metadata and links, returned by paginated API resource collections. Combine with `allOf` and an object that describes `data`.

TelemetryHistory.description: `telemetry-history.v1`: readings bucketed by receipt time, one series per configuration, data type and unit. Empty means no observations, not zero.

from.description: The window actually read, clipped to retention; `null` when the clipped window is empty.

at.description: Start of the bucket, by receipt time.

TelemetryLatest.description: `telemetry-latest.v1`: the retained latest value of each parameter.

configuration_uuid.description: The applied configuration, else the last one the runtime confirmed.

data.description: Empty for a device without a configuration, never zeros.

quality.description: `good`, `invalid` or `stale`; `inactive` when ingestion is disabled and the last valid reading is retained. Receiving it does not make a value fresh.

TelemetryRecords.description: `telemetry-records.v1`: unaggregated good-quality observations, newest first by `(received_at, event_uuid)`. Not a complete export.

from.description: The window actually read, clipped to retention.

consumed.description: Records read so far across pages, up to `limit`.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` with the same query for the next page; `null` on the last page.

TelemetryValue.description: A reading's value; its type follows the parameter's `data_type`.

message.description: The first error, followed by a count of the others.

errors.description: Messages per field, keyed by the field's dotted path. A rejection by the device runtime appears under `runtime`.

applicationToken.description:
Application token for the integration API (`/integration/v1`) only, sent as
`Authorization: Bearer <token>`. An organization administrator issues it for one
application; each application has one active token, valid for 1 to 90 days, whose
abilities are a subset of the application's grants. Session cookies and personal
user tokens are ignored on integration operations.

401 when the token is missing, invalid, expired or revoked; 403 when an ability
the operation needs is not granted on both the application and the token; 404
for another organization or a resource not granted to the application.

session.name: iot-os-session
session.description:
First-party browser session (portal and admin) through Laravel Sanctum.

1. `GET /sanctum/csrf-cookie` (outside `/api`) sets the `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie.
2. `POST /api/v1/auth/login` signs in and sets the session cookie. Its name comes
   from `SESSION_COOKIE`, by default the slug of `APP_NAME` plus `-session`
   (`iot-os-session` in the release profile).
3. Every later request sends the session cookie; unsafe methods (POST, PUT,
   PATCH, DELETE) also send the `XSRF-TOKEN` value in the `X-XSRF-TOKEN` header.

401 without a valid session; 419 when the anti-forgery token is missing or has
expired (fetch `/sanctum/csrf-cookie` again). Application tokens are rejected on
these operations.
